_comment: Sanitized template showing the shape of solo-os-config.json. Onboarding writes the real file for you — you do not normally edit this by hand. No real IDs, emails, or paths here; this is the version that ships in the repo.

voice.name: YOUR FIRST NAME
voice._paths_note: Every path in this block is relative to the project folder that holds solo-os-config.json — 'About Me/voice.md', never 'C:/Users/.../About Me/voice.md'. The config travels with the folder, so an absolute path breaks the moment the folder moves or the OS is installed for someone else. Resolve these against the folder the config was loaded from, not against the working directory.
voice._register_note: Default publishing register: 'linkedin', 'newsletter', or 'none'. Used by polish-and-score only to pick a chain when the asset type is genuinely ambiguous — an explicit target on the draft always wins, and 'none' means ask rather than guess. A user who publishes to both channels leaves this 'none'.
voice._sources_note: voice.sources is the GENERAL voice, applied to every asset. newsletter-voice.md is deliberately NOT listed here — it is a Substack-only register and would bleed into LinkedIn drafting if treated as a general source. It is reached only through newsletter_voice_path.
voice._style_guide_note: anti-ai-writing.md is reached through style_guide_path, NOT through voice.sources. It is an audit-time file: polish-and-score runs it as step 4, the final gate of both chains, and surface-humanizer reads it directly. Listing it in voice.sources as well loads it during drafting too and pays for it twice on every piece — on the reference instance that was ~5,800 tokens, 18% of the stack. Drafting-time word guidance comes from the <avoid> phrase bank in voice.md, a deliberate subset; this file remains the authority and wins at audit.
voice._exemplars_note: voice-exemplars.md holds five complete self-written pieces as few-shot anchors. Read all five; do NOT select the one closest in topic to the draft — topic-matching exemplars measurably reduces voice fidelity. Five is the ceiling, not a floor: fidelity flattens after five and a sixth only costs context. Where an exemplar contradicts a law in voice.md, the exemplar wins.
voice._newsletter_voice_note: Substack register only. Applied by polish-and-score step 3 on newsletter issues; never on a LinkedIn post. The file is tuned across published issues, not generated — if it is missing on an instance that has published before, restore it rather than regenerating it.

notion.week_plans_page: <weekly plans and wraps page id — parent for both Week plan and Week wrap pages>

internal_engagements._comment: Non-client buckets in the Engagements DB. Every task gets an Engagement; work that isn't client work routes here. These rows carry no Status/Rate/Billing model, which is what keeps them out of revenue reporting and the Status=Active views. Onboarding creates the four rows and populates these IDs — you do not fill them in by hand. Routing rules: references/engagement-routing.md.

checkin._comment: Phases of the daily-checkin run. Both default true when absent. run_capture folds the capture skill in as phase 1; render_daybook refreshes the Daybook as phase 3, after the writes.

daybook._comment: Read by render-daybook, and by daily-checkin for the connector probes. Onboarding asks for the timezone in Step 3 and writes this block in Step 4; every other value ships at its default and is edited by hand. artifact_id is written once, on the first successful create_artifact call, and read on every render after that — it is what keeps the artifact link stable.
daybook._artifact_id_note: Leave empty on a fresh install. It MUST end up a kebab-case Cowork artifact slug (mcp__cowork__create_artifact / update_artifact), NOT a claude.ai artifact UUID. Unattended and scheduled sessions do not get the Artifact tool at all, so a UUID here makes every automated render fail with nothing to update.

revenue._comment: source accepts "quickbooks" or "none". This template ships "none" with tiles.revenue false, so a fresh install has zero QuickBooks dependency. Turn both on together if the user wants the tile.

firewall._comment: no_connector_accounts: accounts no connector may act on. walled_engagements: engagement names that must never reach the content vault — not in drafts, not in provenance or sourcing notes, not in the text of a rule describing the wall. Skills read this list; they never name a walled engagement in their own body. Also check that nothing junctions a project folder into the vault root: on Windows, `dir /al <vault root>` lists every junction beside its target, and no recursive scan traverses one.

idea_capture._comment: Step 0 of capture. Sweeps self-addressed idea mail into the content vault, Notion Content Ideas, and Agent Ideas. Requires the content block. Subject grammar and routing table: references/idea-capture-convention.md.

_content_example._note: Optional. Add a 'content' block (this shape, without the underscore) to hook the OS into a content system — the store that holds clips, idea notes, drafts, and the logs. Notion owns tasks and the calendar either way. Enables the standing content deliverables in monday-planner, idea notes in capture (step 5c), the drafts and hygiene checks in friday-wrap, and the content-engine skills (wednesday-synthesis, draft-content, polish-and-score, mark-published, collect-metrics). Omit the block entirely to run the OS without a content pipeline.
_content_example._backend_note: Which store the content skills read and write: 'notion' (databases through the connector — the default, and what a new install should use) or 'vault' (markdown files on disk, the legacy option you opt into). Skills never branch on this themselves. They call the six named operations in references/content-storage.md, and that file gives each operation one vault procedure and one notion procedure — ten skills, one switch, zero half-branches. One backend is live at a time; a skill that reads one store and writes the other corrupts both. A content block present with this key absent is an error, not a default: the skills stop and ask rather than guess a store.

notion._comment: Read only when backend = 'notion'. Onboarding provisions the Clips database and the Theme Map page and writes these IDs. The other content databases are addressed by their existing keys: notion.content_db (Content Calendar) and notion.content_ideas_db (Content Ideas). Clips schema and the field map: references/content-storage.md.

_content_example._vault_paths_note: The ten path keys below are read only when backend = 'vault'. They stay documented here because the vault is a supported backend, not because a new install needs them — a notion install omits them entirely.
_content_example._series_note: The content series in play. Must match the Series select options in the Content Calendar — skills read this list rather than naming series in their own body, so adding a series is a config edit, not a skill edit. A fresh install ships with Standalone only and the user adds their own.

metrics._apify_linkedin_actor_note: Read by collect-metrics only. The account-level post-scorer skill hardcodes the same actor string at its step 2 and does not read this key — change one, change both.

_engagements_example._note: Optional. Add an entry per engagement. Include a weekly_email block to have the Monday planner draft that engagement's weekly email — see skills/monday-planner/references/weekly-email.md. Keep the real 'engagements' list below; this _example key is ignored.
_engagements_example.name: Example Client ERP Migration
